text: The system has identified a pattern that is compatible with a meningioma, but the conformal prediction set also includes an alternative class, so it cannot definitively separate the two possibilities. This ambiguity is understandable because many meningiomas are slow-growing and may appear similar on a single MRI slice, yet their clinical significance varies according to location, size, growth rate and histological grade, factors that cannot be resolved from one study alone [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. A single-image AI model also cannot assess growth over time or determine tumour grade, both of which influence management decisions [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. It is therefore appropriate to discuss further assessment with a qualified clinician, which may include a detailed neurological examination, dedicated contrast-enhanced MRI using a brain-tumour protocol, specialist review and, where tissue is obtained, histological grading [nci-meningioma] [ncbi-meningioma-statpearls]. Ongoing specialist input will guide whether observation, surgical or radiotherapy options, or supportive care are most suitable, and will determine the need for serial imaging and reassessment if symptoms evolve [nci-meningioma] [icom-meningioma-consensus].
